text.p: Italian bonds and futures closed weaker but off lows after a volatile session marked by worries over Italy's early EMU membership.
The June Btp Liffe contract ended 55 basis points down at 127.82 after a low of 127.60.

The market had been in negative territory all day and took a dive when an Italian parliament commission voted against the government's proposed 1997 mini-budget. "The news itself was quickly absorbed but reinforced signs of market vulnerability," one trader said. "We need to see now if Btps manage to stay above 127.60/70 support, if not then it's down to 127.20."
